identity.informationGoal: Explain a long-form editorial subject through a continuous spatial journey while keeping reading and navigation primary.
identity.composition: A full-viewport WebGL world sits behind seven materially different editorial chapters: an opening field, a 2D-to-3D source transformation, an embedded horizontal traverse, and a sequence of photographic, archival, typographic, particle, map, and closing compositions.
identity.interaction: Native vertical wheel, touch, and keyboard scrolling drive one continuous story state. One declared chapter maps vertical travel into a reversible horizontal editorial traverse without capturing or replacing native scrolling.
identity.semantic3d: The opening source image becomes displaced terrain; camera movement reveals the same spatial system from new evidence-bearing viewpoints; later particle and material states explain the active chapter rather than acting as a decorative viewer.

invariants: The document remains an information website with readable headings, body copy, facts, captions, and route navigation.
Every chapter has a distinct composition role; changing only navigation or copy placement is not sufficient.
The 2D source image and the 3D terrain are two states of the same subject and must morph continuously.
The vertical-to-horizontal traverse remains scrubbed by native document progress and is reversible at every point.
Adjacent camera trajectories share an explicit boundary keyframe; camera position and gaze cannot switch formulas on different endpoints.
No important copy or control is accidentally obscured by WebGL, images, or transitional panels.
Desktop and mobile use separately authored camera paths and compositions.
Reduced motion disables smoothing and exposes every chapter in a stable readable state.

stateModel.globalProgress: A clamped 0-to-1 value derived from the complete document scroll range.
stateModel.chapterLocal: Each chapter derives a clamped local progress from its own scroll travel.
stateModel.chapterPresence: A reversible eased value controls chapter visibility and lets neighboring chapters blend without a one-frame swap.
stateModel.horizontalTraverse: The declared traverse chapter maps local progress to a multi-viewport horizontal track and the corresponding camera path.
stateModel.restore: Refresh, resize, locale change, and reverse scroll reconstruct the same semantic chapter from document position.

layers.role: fixed WebGL terrain, river, particles, atmosphere, and semantic transforms
photographic fields, masks, grids, and archival surfaces
chapter headings, explanatory copy, data, captions, and evidence
route progress, map, locale, focus, and accessibility controls

inputs.wheel: Uses native vertical page scroll. A smoothing adapter may interpolate position but must not create a second scroll owner.
inputs.touch: Keeps native vertical momentum and reading order; the horizontal traverse is still driven by vertical document progress.
inputs.keyboard: PageUp, PageDown, arrows, Home, End, Tab, and Escape retain native or clearly labeled behavior.
inputs.pointer: Optional bounded parallax may enrich depth but cannot block selection, links, or semantic progression.

sourceToTraverse.rule: The source trajectory end equals the traverse trajectory start for both camera position and look-at target.
sourceToTraverse.smoothing: Position and gaze use delta-time damping after interpolation.
sourceToTraverse.failure: Any one-frame camera, gaze, background, or chapter-content jump at the boundary.

verticalToHorizontal.rule: Track translation and 3D traversal share the same chapter-local progress and ease family.
verticalToHorizontal.failure: The track stalls, jumps, or moves independently from the world.

transitions.reversibility: All transitions must produce the corresponding previous state when scrolling backward.

responsive.desktop: Uses broad overlap, large type, photographic slices, and a long horizontal traverse with an independently authored camera path.
responsive.mobile: Linearizes reading order, reduces subject travel, repositions images below primary copy, and uses a separate camera boundary and traverse path.
responsive.breakpointPolicy: Interpolate inside each layout mode and switch between separately authored desktop and mobile states at a declared breakpoint.

reducedMotion.behavior: Disable the smoothing controller and continuous decorative time motion; map scroll directly to stable semantic states with short or absent opacity blends.
reducedMotion.required: Every heading, paragraph, fact, caption, route control, and chapter remains reachable and understandable.
